title: Understanding Your Health Insurance

en.description: Questions to ask about your child's health insurance, and where to get help with coverage at Mass General and in Massachusetts.

content.markdown:
Health insurance isn’t the most exciting subject, but it is easily one of the most important. Here are some key questions to consider and resources you will need when planning for your child’s health care coverage.

## Find out which health insurance covers your child right now

- What is the name of your child’s insurance company?
- Is it through a parent’s job, or is it a state or federal plan like MassHealth (Medicaid)?
- If your child is a teen or young adult: how long can they stay on a parent’s plan, and will their coverage change as they get older?

## Find out what your child’s health insurance covers

- Does it cover the doctors your child needs to see?
- Does it cover the procedures your child needs to have?
- Does it cover the medications your child needs to take?

## Find out what your health insurance costs

- What is the premium (the amount you pay each month toward the cost of the insurance policy)?
- Does it have a deductible (the amount you have to pay for your medical care each year before the insurance will begin to cover your costs)?
- How much are the co-pays (the amount you pay at each visit and for each prescription)?

## Help at Mass General

Visit a patient financial counselor at your hospital or health center.

### Patient Financial Services

MGH Yawkey, 2nd Floor, Room 2A

- 55 Fruit Street, Boston, MA 02114
- 📞 [617-726-2191](tel:+16177262191)

## Massachusetts insurance programs

If you live in Massachusetts, you may be able to get health insurance or help paying your health care bills through a state program like MassHealth, the Health Connector, or Health Safety Net. Each program has different rules and income limits.

es.description: Preguntas sobre el seguro médico de su hijo y dónde obtener ayuda con la cobertura en Mass General y en Massachusetts.

content.markdown:
El seguro médico no es el tema más emocionante, pero sin duda es uno de los más importantes. Estas son algunas preguntas clave que debe considerar y los recursos que necesitará al planificar la cobertura médica de su hijo.

## Averigüe qué seguro médico cubre a su hijo ahora

- ¿Cuál es el nombre de la compañía de seguro de su hijo?
- ¿Es a través del trabajo de uno de los padres, o es un plan estatal o federal como MassHealth (Medicaid)?
- Si su hijo es adolescente o adulto joven: ¿cuánto tiempo puede seguir en el plan de uno de sus padres, y cambiará su cobertura a medida que crezca?

## Averigüe qué cubre el seguro médico de su hijo

- ¿Cubre a los médicos que su hijo necesita ver?
- ¿Cubre los procedimientos que su hijo necesita?
- ¿Cubre los medicamentos que su hijo necesita tomar?

## Averigüe cuánto cuesta su seguro médico

- ¿Cuál es la prima (la cantidad que paga cada mes por el costo de la póliza de seguro)?
- ¿Tiene un deducible (la cantidad que tiene que pagar por su atención médica cada año antes de que el seguro empiece a cubrir sus costos)?
- ¿Cuánto son los copagos (la cantidad que paga en cada visita y por cada receta)?

## Ayuda en Mass General

Visite a un consejero financiero para pacientes en su hospital o centro de salud.

### Servicios Financieros para Pacientes

MGH Yawkey, 2do Piso, Sala 2A

- 55 Fruit Street, Boston, MA 02114
- 📞 [617-726-2191](tel:+16177262191)

## Programas de seguro médico de Massachusetts

Si vive en Massachusetts, puede obtener seguro médico o ayuda para pagar sus facturas de atención médica a través de un programa estatal como MassHealth, el Health Connector, o Health Safety Net. Cada programa tiene diferentes reglas y límites de ingresos.

content.label: MassHealth
Massachusetts Health Connector
Health Safety Net
Mass Compare Care

title: Financial Services

en.description: Get answers to billing questions, pay your bill, and contact the Patient Billing Solutions department at Mass General Brigham.

content.markdown:
Get answers to billing questions, pay your bill, and contact our Patient Billing Solutions department.

### Patient Billing Solutions

- 📞 [617-726-3884](tel:+16177263884)
- ✉️ [patientbilling@partners.org](mailto:patientbilling@partners.org) (General questions only)
- 🌐 [massgeneralbrigham.org/en/patients-visitors/billing-insurance/billing](https://www.massgeneralbrigham.org/en/patients-visitors/billing-insurance/billing)

Monday–Wednesday and Friday, 8:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m. Thursday, 9:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m.

## About your bill

For your convenience, Mass General Brigham provides you with one bill. Services provided by private practices affiliated with Mass General Brigham (formerly Partners HealthCare) will be sent to you in a separate bill from those practices.

Patients are billed as soon as possible after their visit or hospital stay. Bill cycles are every 30 days. Bills are not sent until all insurance claims have been processed for that visit.

Once a bill is received, patients are given 25 days to pay their bills in full. The due date will be noted on your bill.

## Payment plans and financial assistance

Mass General Brigham can arrange flexible payment options (payment plans) upon request. If you have medical bills for which you cannot pay, please visit our Financial Assistance page to learn more about options available to you.

content.label: Financial assistance — Mass General Brigham

content.markdown:
## Pay your bill

**Online.** If you have a Patient Gateway account, you can see the current status of all open patient balances; payments are immediately posted to your account. You can opt to go paperless and receive your bills online. You also can set up monthly payment plans. You can pay through Patient Gateway or pay as a guest.

content.label: Pay through Patient Gateway
Pay as a guest

content.markdown: **By phone.** You can also call and press 1 to pay your bill by phone. Please have your account number and the patient's date of birth ready.

content.label: Pay your bill by phone
content.description: Press 1

content.markdown:
**By mail.** Send a check or money order to:

Mass General Brigham
P.O. Box 418393
Boston, MA 02241-8393

Include the coupon from the statement and write your account number (not medical record number) on your check.

es.description: Obtenga respuestas a preguntas sobre facturación, pague su factura y comuníquese con nuestro departamento de Soluciones de Facturación para Pacientes.

content.markdown:
Obtenga respuestas a preguntas sobre facturación, pague su factura y comuníquese con nuestro departamento de Soluciones de Facturación para Pacientes.

### Soluciones de Facturación para Pacientes

- 📞 [617-726-3884](tel:+16177263884)
- ✉️ [patientbilling@partners.org](mailto:patientbilling@partners.org) (Preguntas generales solamente)
- 🌐 [massgeneralbrigham.org/es/patients-visitors/billing-insurance/billing](https://www.massgeneralbrigham.org/es/patients-visitors/billing-insurance/billing)

Lunes a miércoles y viernes, 8:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m. Jueves, 9:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m.

## Acerca de su factura

Para su conveniencia, Mass General Brigham le proporciona una sola factura. Los servicios proporcionados por prácticas privadas afiliadas a Mass General Brigham (anteriormente Partners HealthCare) se le enviarán en una factura separada de esas prácticas.

Los pacientes son facturados tan pronto como sea posible después de su visita o estancia en el hospital. Los ciclos de facturación son cada 30 días. Las facturas no se envían hasta que se hayan procesado todas las reclamaciones del seguro para esa visita.

Una vez que se recibe una factura, se les da a los pacientes 25 días para pagar sus facturas en su totalidad. La fecha de vencimiento se indicará en su factura.

## Planes de pago y asistencia financiera

Mass General Brigham puede organizar opciones de pago flexibles (planes de pago) a solicitud. Si tiene facturas médicas que no puede pagar, visite nuestra página de Asistencia Financiera para obtener más información sobre las opciones disponibles para usted.

content.label: Asistencia financiera — Mass General Brigham

content.markdown:
## Pague su factura

**En línea.** Si tiene una cuenta de Patient Gateway, puede ver el estado actual de todos los saldos de pacientes abiertos; los pagos se publican inmediatamente en su cuenta. Puede optar por recibir sus facturas electrónicamente y no en papel. También puede configurar planes de pago mensuales. Puede pagar a través de Patient Gateway o pagar como invitado.

content.label: Pagar a través de Patient Gateway
Pagar como invitado

content.markdown: **Por teléfono.** También puede llamar y presionar 1 para pagar su factura por teléfono. Tenga su número de cuenta y la fecha de nacimiento del paciente listos.

content.label: Pague su factura por teléfono
content.description: Presione 1

content.markdown:
**Por correo.** Envíe un cheque o giro postal a:

Mass General Brigham
P.O. Box 418393
Boston, MA 02241-8393

Incluya el cupón del estado de cuenta y escriba su número de cuenta (no el número de historial médico) en su cheque.

title: Medical Interpreter Services

en.description: Mass General Brigham hospitals offer language access services 24 hours a day, at no cost, to patients and their family members.

content.markdown:
Mass General Brigham hospitals offer language access services 24 hours a day, at no cost, to patients and their family members. These services include both translation and interpreter services for families and patients to participate fully in their treatment.

Please let your care team know about your communication needs before or during your appointment. If you are scheduling a visit, you may also request an interpreter at that time.

### Interpreter Services at Massachusetts General Hospital

- 📞 [617-726-6966](tel:+16177266966) (Press 6 to speak with a coordinator)
- 🌐 [massgeneralbrigham.org/en/patients-visitors/resources/patient-experience/language-access-services](https://www.massgeneralbrigham.org/en/patients-visitors/resources/patient-experience/language-access-services)

Spanish, Portuguese, and American Sign Language overnight on-call interpreters are available to be paged.

## Spoken language interpreters

We have language interpreters who speak more than 300 languages. Our trained interpreters can join your appointment in person or by phone or video connection. To request an interpreter, please tell your care team or mention your communication needs when scheduling a visit.

## For patients who are Deaf, DeafBlind, or hard of hearing

Our ASL interpreters help patients who are Deaf, DeafBlind, or hard of hearing. Patients also have access to assistive technologies, including videophones, amplified headsets, and CART (Communication Access Realtime Translation) services. If you need one of these resources, please inform your care team before your visit or at check-in.

## Need other accessibility support?

We're committed to ensuring our facilities, services, and information are accessible to all patients, visitors, and staff.

content.label: Accessibility — Mass General Brigham

es.description: Los hospitales de Mass General Brigham ofrecen servicios de acceso lingüístico las 24 horas del día, sin costo, a pacientes y familiares.

content.markdown:
Los hospitales de Mass General Brigham ofrecen servicios de acceso lingüístico las 24 horas del día, sin costo, a pacientes y familiares. Estos servicios incluyen traducción e interpretación para que los pacientes y sus familias participen plenamente en su tratamiento.

Informe a su equipo de atención sobre sus necesidades de comunicación antes de la cita o durante esta. Si está agendando una visita, también puede solicitar un intérprete en ese momento.

### Interpreter Services en Massachusetts General Hospital

- 📞 [617-726-6966](tel:+16177266966) (Marque 6 para hablar con una persona coordinadora)
- 🌐 [massgeneralbrigham.org/es/patients-visitors/resources/patient-experience/language-access-services](https://www.massgeneralbrigham.org/es/patients-visitors/resources/patient-experience/language-access-services)

El horario de atención es de lunes a viernes, de 7 a.m. a 8 p.m., y los sábados y domingos, de 8:00 a.m. a 6:30 p.m.

Durante la noche, hay intérpretes de guardia de español, portugués y lengua de señas estadounidense disponibles mediante buscapersonas.

## Intérpretes de idiomas hablados

Contamos con intérpretes que hablan más de 300 idiomas. Nuestro personal de interpretación capacitado puede participar en su cita en persona, por teléfono o mediante videoconferencia. Para solicitar un intérprete, informe a su equipo de atención o mencione sus necesidades de comunicación cuando agende una visita.

## Para pacientes sordos, sordociegos o con dificultades auditivas

Nuestro personal de interpretación de ASL ayuda a pacientes sordos, sordociegos o con dificultades auditivas. Los pacientes también tienen acceso a tecnologías de asistencia, incluidos videoteléfonos, auriculares amplificados y servicios de CART (traducción en tiempo real para acceso a la comunicación). Si necesita alguno de estos recursos, informe a su equipo de atención antes de la visita o al registrarse.

## ¿Necesita otro tipo de apoyo de accesibilidad?

Nos comprometemos a garantizar que nuestras instalaciones, servicios e información sean accesibles para todos los pacientes, visitantes y miembros del personal.

content.label: Accesibilidad — Mass General Brigham

title: Patient Gateway

en.description: Schedule appointments, participate in virtual visits, renew prescriptions, and more through our secure electronic portal.

content.markdown:
### Mass General Brigham Patient Gateway

- 🌐 [Log in or enroll](https://patientgateway.massgeneralbrigham.org/)
- 🌐 [iOS app](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/patient-gateway/id1175078347)
- 🌐 [Android app](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.partners.ppgmob)

Mass General Brigham Patient Gateway is a secure electronic portal that helps you better manage your own health or the health of a family member. Patient Gateway allows you to do these things and more:

- Communicate with your health care team
- Schedule appointments
- Participate in virtual visits
- Review your medications and renew prescriptions
- View lab or test results
- Read visit notes and after-visit summaries
- Request referrals
- Pay your bill
- Read health and wellness information

Parents, guardians, and adult children also can take advantage of these features to coordinate care for children, dependents, or parents.

Patient Gateway is available in English, Arabic, Traditional Chinese, Haitian Creole, Portuguese, Russian, and Spanish.

## During a hospital stay

If you are admitted to one of our hospitals as an inpatient, you can see important information about your hospital stay. This information includes your inpatient medication list, who is on your care team and their progress notes, and education materials.

## Access to your child's account

A Patient Gateway patient care representative (PCR) account can be set up for patients. A Patient Gateway PCR is not the same thing as a health care proxy. A spouse, parent, adult child, or other designee may become a Patient Gateway PCR if they have been authorized by the patient. Please note that Patient Gateway access for teens and their PCR is limited to meet state regulations for confidential teen care.

Parents or legal guardians can set up a Patient Care Representative (PCR) account to see their child's health records in Patient Gateway. There are 3 ways to request access:

1. Log in to Patient Gateway and fill out the PCR access request form.
2. Request access during an appointment.
3. Call Technical Support.

Legal guardians must provide documentation of guardianship before access is approved.

**Children (ages 0–12):** PCR has full access to the child's health records. But once the child turns 13, access will become limited. This is to protect your teen's privacy and confidentiality, which is required by Massachusetts state law.

**Teens (ages 13–17):** PCR can see all records from ages 0–12. However, PCR access to teens is limited. An example of information that is not shared is anything related to sexual activity/contraception.

When the teen turns 18, PCR access ends automatically.

content.label: Patient Gateway Technical Support
content.description: Help with enrolling, logging in, or setting up access to your child's account.

content.label: Patient Gateway Access for Parents/Guardians (PDF)
content.description: Mass General Brigham's one-page guide to parent access by age.

content.markdown:
## How to use Patient Gateway

Patient Gateway is best used to make simple requests or review your health information. Here are some examples of appropriate and inappropriate use of Patient Gateway:

Do use Patient Gateway to:

- Request non-urgent prescription refills.
- Request scheduling of non-urgent appointments.
- Send photos or information for the care team to review before an appointment.
- View bills and make payments.
- Securely message your care team for non-urgent medical concerns.
- View health information, such as your medication list, test results, and screening tests you might be due for.

Do NOT use Patient Gateway to:

- Make any urgent requests or ask urgent questions. Please contact the office with any urgent needs.
- Send social or personal conversations, photos, and videos that are not related to health care.
- Discuss complex medical issues or new severe medical symptoms. These are often best addressed in a visit with your provider or care team.
- Ask questions about family members from your own Patient Gateway account.
- Make complaints about other providers or care experiences. If you have concerns about your experience, please contact the patient relations office for the clinic or hospital.

es.description: Agende citas, participe en visitas virtuales, renueve recetas y mucho más mediante nuestro portal electrónico seguro.

content.markdown:
### Mass General Brigham Patient Gateway

- 🌐 [Inicie sesión o inscríbase](https://patientgateway.massgeneralbrigham.org/)
- 🌐 [Aplicación para iOS](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/patient-gateway/id1175078347)
- 🌐 [Aplicación para Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=org.partners.ppgmob)

Patient Gateway de Mass General Brigham es un portal electrónico seguro que le ayuda a gestionar mejor su salud o la de un familiar. Patient Gateway le permite hacer lo siguiente y mucho más:

- Comunicarse con su equipo de atención médica
- Agendar citas
- Participar en visitas virtuales
- Revisar sus medicamentos y renovar recetas
- Ver resultados de laboratorio o pruebas
- Leer notas de las visitas y resúmenes posteriores a las visitas
- Solicitar referidos
- Pagar su factura
- Leer información sobre salud y bienestar

Las madres, los padres, las personas tutoras y los hijos adultos también pueden usar estas funciones para coordinar la atención de niños, personas dependientes o padres.

Patient Gateway está disponible en inglés, árabe, chino tradicional, criollo haitiano, portugués, ruso y español.

## Durante una hospitalización

Si ingresa en uno de nuestros hospitales como paciente hospitalizado, podrá ver información importante sobre su hospitalización. Esta información incluye su lista de medicamentos durante la hospitalización, los integrantes de su equipo de atención y sus notas de evolución, además de materiales educativos.

## Acceso a la cuenta de su hijo

Se puede configurar una cuenta de representante de atención al paciente (PCR) de Patient Gateway para los pacientes. Un PCR de Patient Gateway no es lo mismo que un apoderado para la atención médica. Un cónyuge, la madre, el padre, un hijo adulto u otra persona designada puede convertirse en PCR de Patient Gateway si el paciente le ha dado autorización. Tenga en cuenta que el acceso a Patient Gateway para adolescentes y sus PCR está limitado para cumplir con las normativas estatales sobre la atención confidencial de adolescentes.

Los padres o tutores legales pueden crear una cuenta de representante de atención al paciente (PCR) para ver los registros médicos de su hijo en Patient Gateway. Hay 3 maneras de solicitar acceso:

1. Inicie sesión en Patient Gateway y complete el formulario de solicitud de acceso de PCR.
2. Solicite acceso durante una cita.
3. Llame a Soporte Técnico.

Los tutores legales deben presentar documentación de la tutela antes de que se apruebe el acceso.

**Niños (de 0 a 12 años):** el PCR tiene acceso completo a los registros médicos del niño. Pero cuando el niño cumple 13 años, el acceso se limita. Esto protege la privacidad y la confidencialidad de su hijo adolescente, como lo exige la ley del estado de Massachusetts.

**Adolescentes (de 13 a 17 años):** el PCR puede ver todos los registros de los 0 a los 12 años. Sin embargo, el acceso del PCR a los registros del adolescente es limitado. Por ejemplo, no se comparte nada relacionado con la actividad sexual o la anticoncepción.

Cuando el adolescente cumple 18 años, el acceso del PCR termina automáticamente.

content.label: Soporte Técnico de Patient Gateway
content.description: Ayuda para inscribirse, iniciar sesión o configurar el acceso a la cuenta de su hijo.

content.label: Acceso a Patient Gateway para padres y tutores (PDF, en inglés)
content.description: La guía de una página de Mass General Brigham sobre el acceso de los padres según la edad.

content.markdown:
## Cómo usar Patient Gateway

Patient Gateway es más adecuado para hacer solicitudes sencillas o consultar su información médica. A continuación, se ofrecen algunos ejemplos de usos apropiados e inapropiados de Patient Gateway:

Use Patient Gateway para lo siguiente:

- Solicitar renovaciones no urgentes de recetas.
- Solicitar que se agenden citas no urgentes.
- Enviar fotografías o información para que el equipo de atención las revise antes de una cita.
- Ver facturas y realizar pagos.
- Enviar mensajes seguros a su equipo de atención sobre inquietudes médicas no urgentes.
- Ver información médica, como su lista de medicamentos, resultados de pruebas y pruebas de detección que quizá deba realizarse.

NO use Patient Gateway para lo siguiente:

- Hacer solicitudes urgentes o formular preguntas urgentes. Comuníquese con el consultorio si tiene alguna necesidad urgente.
- Enviar conversaciones, fotografías o videos sociales o personales que no estén relacionados con la atención médica.
- Hablar sobre problemas médicos complejos o síntomas médicos nuevos y graves. Por lo general, es mejor tratar estos temas durante una visita con su proveedor o equipo de atención.
- Hacer preguntas sobre familiares desde su propia cuenta de Patient Gateway.
- Presentar quejas sobre otros proveedores o experiencias de atención. Si tiene inquietudes sobre su experiencia, comuníquese con la oficina de relaciones con pacientes de la clínica o el hospital.

content.markdown:
At Mass General Brigham for Children, you can access everything from primary care to advanced specialty services, all tailored to the needs of newborns, children, and teens.

Call us to speak with a team member who can help you understand your options and guide you to the care that is right for you.

### Mass General Brigham for Children

- 📞 [888-644-3248](tel:+18886443248)
- 🌐 [massgeneralbrigham.org/en/services/children](https://www.massgeneralbrigham.org/en/services/children)

Whether you're seeking support for a common concern or a complex condition, our pediatric specialists are here to help. Browse our list of services and programs to find the care that's right for your child.

content.label: Mass General Brigham for Children services and programs

content.markdown:
## Request an appointment

Whether you're a new or returning patient, you can request an appointment, find a provider, or get a second opinion, online or by phone.

content.description: Log in to schedule, manage, or view your upcoming appointments.

content.markdown:
Our patient service representatives can help you register as a new patient and schedule appointments.

### Massachusetts General Hospital

- 📞 [866-211-6588](tel:+18662116588) (Patient registration)
- 📞 [866-489-4046](tel:+18664894046) (Insurance referral)
- 🌐 [massgeneralbrigham.org/en/find-care/request-appointment](https://www.massgeneralbrigham.org/en/find-care/request-appointment)

### Prepare for your appointment

Preparing in advance for your appointment can help your visit go smoothly. Please plan to arrive early to complete registration and bring:

- A photo ID
- Your insurance card
- A list of prescription and over-the-counter medications and supplements
- Your medical history, including hospitalizations, procedures, and allergies

## Get a second opinion

Receive a second opinion from a Mass General Brigham specialist without traveling to Boston. Through our Online Second Opinions service, your physician can request a written consultation from one of our renowned experts to confirm a diagnosis or explore treatment options.

If you have received a life-changing diagnosis, have unexplained symptoms, or are unsure about a treatment plan, getting a second opinion can help you make informed decisions about your care.

To request an Online Second Opinion:

- You and your physician must complete the Online Second Opinions registration.
- You and/or your physician should send all medical records, including imaging and pathology reports, to us.

Specialists typically complete a second opinion within 10 business days. Fees for Online Second Opinions depend on the services. Patients are responsible for all fees.

Due to current regulatory constraints, we cannot provide Online Second Opinions to patients living in Connecticut, Iowa, Maine, New Mexico, Ohio, Tennessee, Texas, US Virgin Islands, and Wyoming. If you live in one of these states and would like to schedule an in-person appointment at Mass General Brigham, please contact the clinical department directly.

content.description: Inicie sesión para agendar, gestionar o ver sus próximas citas.

content.markdown:
Nuestros representantes de servicio al paciente pueden ayudarle a registrarse como nuevo paciente y agendar citas.

### Massachusetts General Hospital

- 📞 [866-211-6588](tel:+18662116588) (Registro de pacientes)
- 📞 [866-489-4046](tel:+18664894046) (Referido de seguro)
- 🌐 [massgeneralbrigham.org/es/find-care/request-appointment](https://www.massgeneralbrigham.org/es/find-care/request-appointment)

### Prepárese para su cita

Prepararse con anticipación para su cita puede ayudar a que su visita transcurra sin problemas. Planee llegar temprano para completar el registro y traiga:

- Una identificación con foto
- Su tarjeta de seguro
- Una lista de medicamentos recetados y de venta libre y suplementos
- Su historial médico, incluyendo hospitalizaciones, procedimientos y alergias

## Obtenga una segunda opinión

Reciba una segunda opinión de un especialista de Mass General Brigham sin viajar a Boston. A través de nuestro servicio de Opiniones Secundarias en Línea, su médico puede solicitar una consulta escrita de uno de nuestros renombrados expertos para confirmar un diagnóstico o explorar opciones de tratamiento.

Si recibió un diagnóstico que cambia la vida, presenta síntomas inexplicables o no está seguro acerca de un plan de tratamiento, obtener una segunda opinión puede ayudarle a tomar decisiones informadas sobre su atención.

Para solicitar una Segunda Opinión en Línea:

- Usted y su médico deben completar el registro de la Segunda Opinión en Línea.
- Usted o su médico deben enviar todos los registros médicos, incluyendo informes de imágenes y patología, a nosotros.

Los especialistas generalmente completan una segunda opinión dentro de 10 días hábiles. Las tarifas para las Segundas Opiniones en Línea dependen de los servicios. Los pacientes son responsables de todos los honorarios.

Debido a las restricciones regulatorias actuales, no podemos proporcionar Opiniones Secundarias en línea a pacientes que viven en Connecticut, Iowa, Maine, Nuevo México, Ohio, Tennessee, Texas, Islas Vírgenes de EE. UU., y Wyoming. Si vive en uno de estos estados y desea agendar una cita en persona en Mass General Brigham, contacte directamente al departamento clínico.

At Mass General Brigham for Children, you can access everything from primary care to advanced specialty services, all tailored to the needs of newborns, children, and teens.

Call us to speak with a team member who can help you understand your options and guide you to the care that is right for you.
markdown.es:
En Mass General Brigham para Niños, puede acceder a todo, desde atención primaria hasta servicios especializados avanzados, todos adaptados a las necesidades de recién nacidos, niños y adolescentes.

Llámenos para hablar con un miembro del equipo que puede ayudarle a entender sus opciones y guiarle hacia la atención que es adecuada para usted.

markdown.en: Whether you're seeking support for a common concern or a complex condition, our pediatric specialists are here to help. Browse our list of services and programs to find the care that's right for your child.
markdown.es: Ya sea que esté buscando apoyo para una preocupación común o una condición compleja, nuestros especialistas pediátricos están aquí para ayudar. Consulte nuestra lista de servicios y programas para encontrar la atención adecuada para su hijo.

markdown.en:
### Prepare for your appointment

Preparing in advance for your appointment can help your visit go smoothly. Please plan to arrive early to complete registration and bring:

- A photo ID
- Your insurance card
- A list of prescription and over-the-counter medications and supplements
- Your medical history, including hospitalizations, procedures, and allergies
markdown.es:
### Prepárese para su cita

Prepararse con anticipación para su cita puede ayudar a que su visita transcurra sin problemas. Planee llegar temprano para completar el registro y traiga:

- Una identificación con foto
- Su tarjeta de seguro
- Una lista de medicamentos recetados y de venta libre y suplementos
- Su historial médico, incluyendo hospitalizaciones, procedimientos y alergias

markdown.en:
Receive a second opinion from a Mass General Brigham specialist without traveling to Boston. Through our Online Second Opinions service, your physician can request a written consultation from one of our renowned experts to confirm a diagnosis or explore treatment options.

If you have received a life-changing diagnosis, have unexplained symptoms, or are unsure about a treatment plan, getting a second opinion can help you make informed decisions about your care.

To request an Online Second Opinion:

- You and your physician must complete the Online Second Opinions registration.
- You and/or your physician should send all medical records, including imaging and pathology reports, to us.

Specialists typically complete a second opinion within 10 business days. Fees for Online Second Opinions depend on the services. Patients are responsible for all fees.

Due to current regulatory constraints, we cannot provide Online Second Opinions to patients living in Connecticut, Iowa, Maine, New Mexico, Ohio, Tennessee, Texas, US Virgin Islands, and Wyoming. If you live in one of these states and would like to schedule an in-person appointment at Mass General Brigham, please contact the clinical department directly.
markdown.es:
Reciba una segunda opinión de un especialista de Mass General Brigham sin viajar a Boston. A través de nuestro servicio de Opiniones Secundarias en Línea, su médico puede solicitar una consulta escrita de uno de nuestros renombrados expertos para confirmar un diagnóstico o explorar opciones de tratamiento.

Si recibió un diagnóstico que cambia la vida, presenta síntomas inexplicables o no está seguro acerca de un plan de tratamiento, obtener una segunda opinión puede ayudarle a tomar decisiones informadas sobre su atención.

Para solicitar una Segunda Opinión en Línea:

- Usted y su médico deben completar el registro de la Segunda Opinión en Línea.
- Usted o su médico deben enviar todos los registros médicos, incluyendo informes de imágenes y patología, a nosotros.

Los especialistas generalmente completan una segunda opinión dentro de 10 días hábiles. Las tarifas para las Segundas Opiniones en Línea dependen de los servicios. Los pacientes son responsables de todos los honorarios.

Debido a las restricciones regulatorias actuales, no podemos proporcionar Opiniones Secundarias en línea a pacientes que viven en Connecticut, Iowa, Maine, Nuevo México, Ohio, Tennessee, Texas, Islas Vírgenes de EE. UU., y Wyoming. Si vive en uno de estos estados y desea agendar una cita en persona en Mass General Brigham, contacte directamente al departamento clínico.

title: Quality and Safety

en.description: We strive to be the top health system in the country for quality, informed by data and grounded in safety and equity.

content.markdown:
## What does quality and safety mean for your child?

When you get "outstanding quality" health care, it means your care is based on evidence, family-centered and provided by skilled and knowledgeable professionals who communicate and coordinate the care in a timely way.

You and your child should feel safe at Mass General Brigham for Children, and one of the best ways to improve patient safety is to constantly monitor performance and family experiences to set up systems to provide the best care for your child. The Mass General Brigham for Children Quality and Safety is committed to this work every day.

### High Quality & Safe Care at Mass General Brigham for Children Is:

- Evidence-based
- Family-centered
- Provided by skilled professionals
- Rooted in a culture of open communication and continuous improvement
- Driven by feedback from our families

## Patient safety

It can be difficult for infants and children to communicate their concerns or changes in symptoms. Mass General Brigham for Children offers our patients, families and staff a robust patient safety program which focuses on family participation in care, mitigation of safety risks, teamwork and rapid response to emergencies. We are committed to being a high reliability organization where our systems support patient safety and allow our patients, families and staff to feel free to speak up about patient safety concerns.

Some examples of our Patient Safety initiatives include:

**Safety Culture** — Mass General Brigham for Children is committed to a strong safety culture in which families and staff feel free to raise patient safety concerns and those voiced concerns result in patient safety improvements.

**Rapid Response** — Mass General Brigham for Children Neonatal and Pediatric Rapid Response Teams can be activated for any acute or unexpected clinical concerns. The Rapid Response Team comes to the patient location to assist patients and care teams with their urgent concerns.

**Family-Centered Rounds** — Families are encouraged to participate as team members during morning rounds. This enables parents to actively participate in their child's care planning and provides a time for raising questions or concerns.

Mass General Brigham clinicians and care teams work together every day to deliver the very best patient outcomes, guided by our patient care strategy, For Every Patient.

content.label: Quality, Safety, and Outcomes — Mass General Brigham

es.description: Nos esforzamos por ser el mejor sistema de salud del país en calidad, informado por datos y fundamentado en la seguridad y la equidad.

content.markdown:
## ¿Qué significan la calidad y la seguridad para su hijo?

Recibir atención médica de "calidad excepcional" significa que la atención se basa en evidencia, está centrada en la familia y la brindan profesionales capacitados y con conocimientos que se comunican y coordinan la atención de manera oportuna.

Usted y su hijo deben sentirse seguros en Mass General Brigham para Niños, y una de las mejores maneras de mejorar la seguridad del paciente es supervisar constantemente el desempeño y las experiencias de las familias para establecer sistemas que brinden la mejor atención a su hijo. El equipo de Calidad y Seguridad de Mass General Brigham para Niños se dedica a este trabajo todos los días.

### La atención segura y de alta calidad en Mass General Brigham para Niños es:

- Basada en evidencia
- Centrada en la familia
- Brindada por profesionales capacitados
- Arraigada en una cultura de comunicación abierta y mejora continua
- Guiada por los comentarios de nuestras familias

## Seguridad del paciente

Puede ser difícil para los bebés y los niños comunicar sus preocupaciones o los cambios en sus síntomas. Mass General Brigham para Niños ofrece a nuestros pacientes, familias y personal un sólido programa de seguridad del paciente que se centra en la participación de la familia en la atención, la reducción de los riesgos de seguridad, el trabajo en equipo y la respuesta rápida ante emergencias. Nos comprometemos a ser una organización de alta confiabilidad en la que nuestros sistemas apoyen la seguridad del paciente y permitan que nuestros pacientes, familias y personal se sientan libres de expresar sus preocupaciones sobre la seguridad del paciente.

Algunos ejemplos de nuestras iniciativas de seguridad del paciente son:

**Cultura de seguridad** — Mass General Brigham para Niños está comprometido con una sólida cultura de seguridad en la que las familias y el personal se sienten libres de expresar sus preocupaciones sobre la seguridad del paciente, y esas preocupaciones dan lugar a mejoras en la seguridad del paciente.

**Respuesta rápida** — Los Equipos de Respuesta Rápida Neonatal y Pediátrica de Mass General Brigham para Niños pueden activarse ante cualquier preocupación clínica aguda o inesperada. El Equipo de Respuesta Rápida acude al lugar donde está el paciente para ayudar a los pacientes y a los equipos de atención con sus preocupaciones urgentes.

**Rondas centradas en la familia** — Se anima a las familias a participar como miembros del equipo durante las rondas de la mañana. Esto permite que los padres participen activamente en la planificación de la atención de su hijo y ofrece un momento para hacer preguntas o expresar preocupaciones.

Los clínicos y equipos de atención de Mass General Brigham trabajan juntos todos los días para ofrecer los mejores resultados para los pacientes, guiados por nuestra estrategia de atención al paciente, For Every Patient.

title: PICU Follow-Up Clinic

en.description: Developmental follow-up service supporting former PICU patients through recovery, growth, and ongoing care.

content.markdown:
Mass General Brigham for Children Hospital Discharge Follow Up Clinic is a diverse unit that provides high-quality follow-up service to aid in the development of former PICU patients.

### Hospital Discharge Follow Up Clinic

- 165 Cambridge Street, Floor 5, Boston, MA 02114
- 📞 [617-724-8797](tel:+16177248797)
- 🌐 [massgeneralbrigham.org/en/locations/boston-ma/mass-general-brigham-for-children-hospital-discharge-follow-up-clinic-loc0000280196](https://www.massgeneralbrigham.org/en/locations/boston-ma/mass-general-brigham-for-children-hospital-discharge-follow-up-clinic-loc0000280196)

Patients with appointments at 165, 175, and 185 Cambridge Street should park in the Charles River Plaza garage, with the entrance at 207 Cambridge Street, next to Flour Bakery.

## About Us

For those patients who require its services, our mission is to aid in the critical care post-discharge difficulties that may arise from hospital discharge by providing exceptional service and treatment to the multicultural patients and families we serve. We utilize excellent communication with the family and primary care pediatricians to optimize long-term successful patient outcomes.

The Mass General Brigham for Children PICU provides monitoring and life-sustaining treatment for critically ill patients suffering from a wide range of illnesses. The Mass General Brigham for Children PICU Follow-Up Clinic will focus on evaluating the intensive care patients discharged from the PICU. PICU patients and their families experience a high risk for developing medical, neurodevelopmental, and psychosocial needs related to post-intensive care syndrome. So, it is not uncommon for them to seek out help along this journey. This includes patients who have had a prolonged stay in the PICU for a critical illness.

The Pediatric Intensive Care Unit Follow-Up Clinic is a developmental follow-up service. We support your children through the aid in their development, growth, and recovery for them to reach their full potential.

These issues have commonly been overlooked by health care providers as post-intensive care patients transition care back into the community following their serious illness. The Mass General Brigham for Children PICU Follow-Up Clinic was uniquely designed to combat this issue.

This process can be described in four steps:

## Steps of Patient Care

1. Hospital discharge
2. Evaluate areas of cognition and psychosocial function
3. Neurodevelopment and family functioning to identify ongoing needs, and set up referrals to community providers for ongoing follow-up
4. Support the child and family through the long-term recovery after critical illness

es.description: Servicio de seguimiento del desarrollo que apoya a antiguos pacientes de la PICU en su recuperación, crecimiento y atención continua.

content.markdown:
La Clínica de Seguimiento tras el Alta Hospitalaria de Mass General Brigham para Niños es una unidad diversa que brinda un servicio de seguimiento de alta calidad para ayudar en el desarrollo de antiguos pacientes de la PICU.

### Clínica de Seguimiento tras el Alta Hospitalaria

- 165 Cambridge Street, Floor 5, Boston, MA 02114
- 📞 [617-724-8797](tel:+16177248797)
- 🌐 [massgeneralbrigham.org/en/locations/boston-ma/mass-general-brigham-for-children-hospital-discharge-follow-up-clinic-loc0000280196](https://www.massgeneralbrigham.org/en/locations/boston-ma/mass-general-brigham-for-children-hospital-discharge-follow-up-clinic-loc0000280196)

Si tiene una cita en 165, 175 o 185 Cambridge Street, estacione en el garaje de Charles River Plaza, con entrada en 207 Cambridge Street.

## Sobre nosotros

Para los pacientes que requieren sus servicios, nuestra misión es ayudar con las dificultades que pueden surgir después del alta de cuidados intensivos, brindando un servicio y tratamiento excepcionales a los pacientes y familias multiculturales a quienes servimos. Mantenemos una excelente comunicación con la familia y los pediatras de atención primaria para lograr los mejores resultados a largo plazo para los pacientes.

La PICU de Mass General Brigham para Niños brinda monitoreo y tratamiento de soporte vital a pacientes en estado crítico con una amplia variedad de enfermedades. La Clínica de Seguimiento de la PICU de Mass General Brigham para Niños se centra en evaluar a los pacientes de cuidados intensivos dados de alta de la PICU. Los pacientes de la PICU y sus familias tienen un alto riesgo de desarrollar necesidades médicas, del neurodesarrollo y psicosociales relacionadas con el síndrome posterior a cuidados intensivos. Por eso, no es raro que busquen ayuda a lo largo de este camino. Esto incluye a pacientes que han tenido una estancia prolongada en la PICU por una enfermedad crítica.

La Clínica de Seguimiento de la Unidad de Cuidados Intensivos Pediátricos es un servicio de seguimiento del desarrollo. Apoyamos a sus hijos en su desarrollo, crecimiento y recuperación para que alcancen todo su potencial.

Los profesionales de la salud a menudo han pasado por alto estas necesidades cuando los pacientes que salen de cuidados intensivos regresan a su comunidad después de una enfermedad grave. La Clínica de Seguimiento de la PICU de Mass General Brigham para Niños fue diseñada especialmente para atender este problema.

Este proceso se puede describir en cuatro pasos:

## Pasos de la atención al paciente

1. Alta hospitalaria
2. Evaluar las áreas de cognición y funcionamiento psicosocial
3. Evaluar el neurodesarrollo y el funcionamiento familiar para identificar necesidades continuas, y hacer referidos a proveedores de la comunidad para el seguimiento
4. Apoyar al niño y a la familia durante la recuperación a largo plazo después de una enfermedad crítica

en.description: Why vaccines matter for your child and your community — answers to common parent questions.

content.markdown:
Vaccines can help prevent many diseases that affect children and adults. Some parents are nervous about their children getting vaccines, and that's okay. In this resource, you will learn why vaccines are important for your child's health and your community's health.

## Why should my child get vaccinated?

Vaccines help prevent many diseases that affect children and adults. This includes diseases that are not common, like measles, mumps and rubella, rotavirus and polio. These diseases used to be common, but now they are not — because most children and adults have been vaccinated.

## Why does my child need so many vaccines when they are young?

We give children vaccines as early as possible to protect them from disease. It might seem like a lot, but there is enough time in between each vaccine or dose so your child can build up immunity (resistance) to the disease.

Delaying your child's vaccines means delaying protection against disease. Talk with your child's doctor if you have questions or concerns about your child's vaccine schedule (the time between vaccines).

## How well do vaccines work?

Most vaccines work about 90% of the time. This means that **9 out of 10 children** who get a vaccine will not catch the disease the vaccine protects against. Not every vaccine works all of the time, but many work well for children and adults.

**No.** Studies have not been able to show that vaccines cause autism. The one study that showed vaccines cause autism was retracted (proven to be untrue). Talk with your child's doctor about your concerns or questions. They can tell you more about each vaccine, why it's important, and how it can help your child.

- **It helps lower the number of people affected by a disease.** As more people are vaccinated against a certain disease, the disease affects fewer people over time. This is because most children are vaccinated against measles.

en.description: Room-by-room tips to make your home safer before your baby starts crawling.

content.markdown:
It is exciting when your baby learns to crawl and walk. This is an important time to make your home as safe as possible for your baby. In this resource, you will learn how to childproof your home before your baby learns to crawl.

## What is childproofing your home?

When you childproof your home, you make your home as safe as possible for when your baby arrives. How you childproof your home changes as your baby grows up.

## How long does it take to childproof my home?

Babyproofing changes over time. As your baby grows and develops new skills, you will need to adjust the level of safety in your home.

## How do I childproof my home before my baby learns to crawl?

Babies like to grab onto surfaces, pick up objects, and put them in their mouths. They learn to understand the world around them through touch and taste. Here are tips to childproof your home:

### Kitchen

- When you cook or prepare food, keep your baby in a highchair or safely enclosed play area where you can see them.
- Install locks or stops on drawers, cabinets, switches, the refrigerator door, and oven doors. Keep magnets and other small objects out of your baby's reach.
- Turn pot handles inward on the stove. Use the burners toward the back wall.
- Store household cleaners and poisons in locked cabinets that are out of your baby's reach.
- Keep small appliances and other items away from the edges of countertops or tables.

### Living room, den, and bedrooms

- Attach televisions and heavy furniture, like bookshelves, to the wall. This can help prevent the TV or furniture from falling if your baby bumps into it or pushes on it.
- Secure and hide electrical cords.
- If you have older children, have them put away their toys out of your baby's reach.
- Keep the floors and other surfaces free of items your baby could choke on or break.

### Bathroom and laundry room

- Secure toilet lids.
- Store cleaners, poisons, and laundry products in a locked cabinet out of your child's reach.
- Empty the bathtub or other large containers with liquid as soon as you are done using them.

### Other tips

- Use safety covers in electrical outlets.
- Install safety gates at the top and bottom of every staircase.
- Cover sharp corners on furniture or household objects.
- For more tips, ask the care team or visit the [National Safety Council's childproofing page](https://www.nsc.org/community-safety/safety-topics/child-safety/childproofing-your-home).

> **Did you know?** The best way to childproof your home is to see the world from your baby's point of view. Get down on the floor — or as close as possible — to check for anything your baby could get into.

en.description: Distracted driving causes more than half of teen crashes — what families should know about the law and good habits.

content.markdown:
Driver distraction is responsible for **more than 58% of teen automobile crashes**. Michael Flaherty, DO, of the Pediatric Trauma Service and the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) at MGHfC shares these tips to keep drivers, their families, and the community safe.

## Key Takeaways

- Set mobile electronic devices to **Do Not Disturb** mode, which prevents texts, calls, and notifications from coming through while the user is in a vehicle.
- Set an example for others. Peers, children, and colleagues learn from one another, so we need to make distracted driving an unacceptable behavior.
- Talk with your teenage driver about the dangers of driving while distracted — including the risks of using cell phones, eating, and manipulating the radio while behind the wheel. Remind teens that driving requires all of their attention.

## What is distracted driving?

Distracted driving means your attention or focus is taken away from the task of driving. It comprises three core types:

- **Visual** — when you take your eyes off the road
- **Manual** — when you take your hands off the wheel
- **Cognitive** — when your mind is not primarily focused on driving

Distracted driving is dangerous and can lead to injury and death. **More than 1,000 people are injured daily in crashes involving a distracted driver.** While any distraction can endanger the driver and others, texting while driving is especially dangerous as it combines all three types of distraction. It takes the brain approximately 30 seconds to refocus on driving after looking at a mobile phone.

## What is the law?

The Massachusetts hands-free law prohibits all drivers from all use of their phones, for any reason — including making calls, reading or sending text messages, using social media, or typing in directions — even when at a stop light or in traffic.

## What if I need to use navigation, answer the phone, or make a call?

Drivers can use their mobile device's voice commands for directions and calls — such as Apple's Siri or Google Assistant — which must be enabled to place calls or get directions. Cars without built-in GPS, Apple CarPlay, or Android Auto must be equipped with a phone mount on the dash or windshield for GPS navigation. Drivers must type in their destination and start the directions **before** driving.

If you need to answer or make a phone call, the safest thing to do is pull over to the side of the road or park your car in a safe location.

## What should parents do?

Drivers under the age of 20 have the highest rate of distraction-related fatal crashes. Parents need to foster open conversations about the importance of the law and how it works to ensure their own safety and the safety of others.

Since 2010 it has been illegal in Massachusetts for any junior operator — drivers under age 18 — to talk on the phone in any way while driving, including hands-free.

Encourage teenage drivers to speak up if they see their peers or others driving distracted, just as they would if someone were driving drunk. Parents must also set good examples by not using their phones while driving.

title: Gun Safety: How to Discuss with Any Age Child

en.description: Age-appropriate ways to talk with kids — toddlers to teens — about gun violence and home gun safety.

content.markdown:
*By Gretchen Fischer Felopulos, PhD, and Gene Beresin, Executive Director — MGH Clay Center for Young Healthy Minds*

Recent mass shootings that have made national news headlines are a frightening reminder to us all of this "new normal." Beyond those that have made national headlines, there are many more incidents of gun violence — sometimes more than one a day — for which the trauma is felt only locally.

We emotionally respond to these horrifying incidents with a sense of terror, fear for our own safety, and sadness for the victims and those who loved them. We ask ourselves: was it yet another random act of violence by a troubled individual, or was it inspired by hateful voices that fueled the flames of someone who felt alone, angry, and marginalized?

Beyond our immediate gut reactions, we can expect media coverage to extend across our televisions, radios, computers, and mobile devices, as in any crisis. And we can expect that our kids, teenagers, and young adults will have varying levels of information about these tragic events, along with their own emotional reactions, questions, and concerns.

How can parents, educators, and other caring adults help our young people process acts of gun violence in this moment, when we know they already feel vulnerable? How can we help them live with confidence and self-assurance in the world without constant fear that their everyday life is filled with imminent danger? How can we help them put these tragedies into some perspective?

As with any of our caregiver guidelines, first remember that you know your child best. Then, the approach for each child should be developmentally appropriate. What helps a 7-year-old cope with fear and anxiety may not be the same for a 17-year-old.

Below are some basic tips for how to talk with a child of any age about gun violence.

## Talking Tips for All Ages

**Control your own anxiety.** Let's face it — we are all scared about gun violence. Anxiety is contagious, and your kids will know this. If they ask you directly, be honest and say you are rattled by recent shootings, and express how terrible you feel for these losses and for the victims' families and communities.

**Use self-care measures to calm yourself down.** Research shows that when a parent is calm and under control, they are in the best position to talk with their kids about scary things.

**Talk with other adults you trust about gun violence and hate crimes.** Sometimes partners, friends, family, clergy, or community leaders will help you clarify your own reactions and help you contain your anxiety.

**Be proactive.** Limit your own exposure to gun violence by turning off the news coverage and avoiding social media posts focused on violent events. While it is important to stay informed, repeatedly viewing the news stories and related content tends to add to our fears, not reduce them.

**Keep your own home safe from gun violence.** Around one in three homes with children contains at least one firearm, so it is critical for gun-owning parents to safely store them away — ideally by locking up the unloaded gun and storing the ammunition in a separate locked location. If you think your children don't know where you keep your guns, or that they know not to play with them, think again. Research and past experience have shown that too many accidental shootings occur in the home by making these assumptions.

**Talk with your kids about gun safety rules.** If you have guns in the home, be sure to talk with your children of any age about gun safety rules. No child should be able to have any access to firearms without adult supervision. If you have not developed and discussed family rules about the storage, access, and use of firearms, establish them, post them, and have a serious conversation about your rules. Even if you don't have guns in your home, it is possible that there are firearms at a friend's home — so it is key that you talk with your young people about gun safety. The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends that you ask parents about their own gun safety practices before your child attends a playdate, party, or sleepover at their home.

## Talking Tips by Age Group

### Toddlers and Preschoolers

**Very young children are more disturbed by their parents' and caregivers' distress than by the actual event.** They may not fully understand what happened, or they may see it as more than an act on TV. That's why they're comforted more by your actions than your words. Be careful how you present yourself to them, both emotionally and in conversation with others. Naturally, they will pick up on your reactions.

**Expect young children to regress a bit emotionally.** They may become clingy or whiny, have difficulty sleeping, or start wetting their beds. The more patient and reassuring you are, the more quickly these episodes will pass.

**Turn off the media.** Young children have no idea where distant cities are, and may think the events happened right near their homes. Let them know that these places are far away. If you wish to watch or listen to news coverage, do so while your very young children are not in the room; they do not yet have the ability to put the frightening images they see into perspective. If you have conversations about shootings with a partner or older children at home, be sure they are not within earshot.

### Grade School Children

**Encourage your school-aged children to share their feelings and concerns with you.** Certainly, they will have heard about recent events. Assure them that it's all right for them to be upset, and that you'll do everything you can to protect them from harm.

**Ask what specifically worries them** and what they know about recent shootings. Also, ask where they heard about it — it is very important to know where they get their information.

**If appropriate, reassure them that you live in a very safe place** and that these events are not common — though you do need to admit that they are very scary.

**Remember that children often work through emotional issues with play instead of words.** Don't be surprised if your children use toys to replay the images they've seen or imagined. This is healthy. It can also give you insights into their fears and misunderstandings.

**Expect that your children might ask the same questions several times.** Be patient. By asking these questions, they're showing you that they trust you and what you say.

**Turn off the media.** It is not wise for school-aged kids to follow news coverage of these events. However, if they have already seen or heard about the breaking news, be available to clarify their concerns.

**Remind them:** there are more good people in the world than there are bad people, and the good people will always try to take care of and protect them.

**Talk about angry feelings and how to manage them.** Even school-aged kids know that children and adults get angry and have conflicts, and they have probably seen all sorts of violence in movies, on TV, and in real life. Discuss how anger can be managed, and explain that there is never reason to manage anger with violence.

### Teenagers and Young Adults

Adolescents may be scared and wonder what this means for the lives they'll lead as young adults. For example, "Will I be safe in college, or in the community where I live and work?" They may struggle with questions about justice, power, and the use of weapons — issues that directly relate to violent events. And as parents, young people of color or other marginalized individuals may be particularly worried.

Teenagers are capable of having nuanced discussions and considering issues, values, motives, and consequent behavior — appropriate and unacceptable.

**Let your teenagers listen as you discuss the event with other adults.** If they choose to chime in, welcome their participation — even if you might disagree with what they have to say. Simply talking things out will help them to put their concerns into perspective.

**Sit with them as they watch the news coverage.** Comment on what you're seeing, and listen openly to what they have to say, as well. Encourage them to limit their time spent on related content — for many people, this only adds to their fears.

**Share your feelings with them.** This gives adolescents permission to do the same with you. Share your feelings about mass shootings, the targets of the shootings, and issues with use and misuse of firearms. Ask about their feelings about these issues.

**Discuss the risks of access to guns.** Teens are capable of discussing how many guns we have in our nation and whether this is safe or dangerous for society, as well as talking about factors that contribute to gun violence — such as domestic abuse, drugs and alcohol, and mental health issues like depression. Access to a gun is one of the biggest risk factors on the list. Engage in conversations about how reduction of firearms and "red flag" laws have been shown to prevent personal violence (suicide) and reduce rates of homicide and mass shootings.

**Talk with them about appropriate gun use and gun safety.** Teens are old enough to appreciate that firearms in the hands of an angry, impulsive person are dangerous. Talk with them about the appropriate use of firearms — such as for hunting, skeet shooting, target shooting, and on rare occasions, for self-defense.

**Ask them about their opinion on assault rifles.** Talk with them about why anyone would use one. They are not used for hunting or for sport. Is there any time or reason someone would need to use one?

**Ask them about their opinion of copycat phenomena.** Wonder with them about how media coverage of shootings affects people's feelings, and whether they think some might copy the event, or react negatively.

**Wonder about risks to people of color.** Research shows that people of color are at a much greater risk of being shot or killed by guns. Ask your teens and young adults how people of color, Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders, and other marginalized people such as the LGBTQ population are at greater risk for violence of all sorts.

---

We desperately need to keep our children and society safe. We need action to prevent more devastating events. With 40,000 gun-related deaths in our country per year, this is a public health crisis and our children are at risk.

One important role we have in preventing needless death by firearms — besides state and national legislation — is having conversations with our youth to help them feel safe and be part of the solution when they become leaders in the future.

**Talk about angry feelings and how to manage them.** Even school-aged kids know that children and adults get angry and have conflicts, and they have probably seen all sorts of violence in movies, on TV, and in real life. Discuss how anger can be managed, and explain that there is never reason to manage anger with violence.

### Teenagers and Young Adults

Adolescents may be scared and wonder what this means for the lives they'll lead as young adults. For example, "Will I be safe in college, or in the community where I live and work?" They may struggle with questions about justice, power, and the use of weapons — issues that directly relate to violent events. And as parents, young people of color or other marginalized individuals may be particularly worried.

Teenagers are capable of having nuanced discussions and considering issues, values, motives, and consequent behavior — appropriate and unacceptable.

**Let your teenagers listen as you discuss the event with other adults.** If they choose to chime in, welcome their participation — even if you might disagree with what they have to say. Simply talking things out will help them to put their concerns into perspective.

**Sit with them as they watch the news coverage.** Comment on what you're seeing, and listen openly to what they have to say, as well. Encourage them to limit their time spent on related content — for many people, this only adds to their fears.

**Share your feelings with them.** This gives adolescents permission to do the same with you. Share your feelings about mass shootings, the targets of the shootings, and issues with use and misuse of firearms. Ask about their feelings about these issues.

**Discuss the risks of access to guns.** Teens are capable of discussing how many guns we have in our nation and whether this is safe or dangerous for society, as well as talking about factors that contribute to gun violence — such as domestic abuse, drugs and alcohol, and mental health issues like depression. Access to a gun is one of the biggest risk factors on the list. Engage in conversations about how reduction of firearms and "red flag" laws have been shown to prevent personal violence (suicide) and reduce rates of homicide and mass shootings.

**Talk with them about appropriate gun use and gun safety.** Teens are old enough to appreciate that firearms in the hands of an angry, impulsive person are dangerous. Talk with them about the appropriate use of firearms — such as for hunting, skeet shooting, target shooting, and on rare occasions, for self-defense.

**Ask them about their opinion on assault rifles.** Talk with them about why anyone would use one. They are not used for hunting or for sport. Is there any time or reason someone would need to use one?

**Ask them about their opinion of copycat phenomena.** Wonder with them about how media coverage of shootings affects people's feelings, and whether they think some might copy the event, or react negatively.

**Wonder about risks to people of color.** Research shows that people of color are at a much greater risk of being shot or killed by guns. Ask your teens and young adults how people of color, Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders, and other marginalized people such as the LGBTQ population are at greater risk for violence of all sorts.

---

We desperately need to keep our children and society safe. We need action to prevent more devastating events. With 40,000 gun-related deaths in our country per year, this is a public health crisis and our children are at risk.

One important role we have in preventing needless death by firearms — besides state and national legislation — is having conversations with our youth to help them feel safe and be part of the solution when they become leaders in the future.

title: Guardianship: What You Need to Know

en.description: How guardianship works for adults over 18 who are incapacitated — types of guardians, alternatives, and effects on health care.

content.markdown:
You may have many questions about guardianship and health care. In this resource, you will learn how guardianship affects health care for adults over age 18 who are incapacitated. You will also learn about the different types of guardians and related roles.

## What is a legal guardian?

A legal guardian is a person (or people) named by the Probate and Family Court who is responsible for another adult's support, protection, and wellbeing when the court finds that an adult is incapacitated (cannot make informed decisions for themselves). This includes decisions around major areas of life, like medical care and housing. The court might also name a legal conservator. This person makes decisions around legal paperwork. Both guardians and conservators help the adult in their care with public benefits and services, general welfare, and planning for the future.

## Which paperwork gives the details of guardianship?

The Probate and Family Court provides the legal paperwork. The paperwork is called the **Decree and Order**. It includes information about the guardian and/or conservator, and the limits of their roles.

## At what age does a child become their own legal guardian?

Children become their own legal guardians at age 18. This means they are legal adults — even if they are incapacitated. For this reason, it is important to get legal guardianship before the person turns 18 if they are incapacitated.

## Why does an adult need a guardian?

Adults need a guardian when the court finds that the person is incapacitated. This means they cannot make informed decisions on their own.

To be incapacitated, adults must:

- Be at least 18 years old
- Have a doctor's diagnosis of incapacitation
- Be unable to assess or communicate medical information or make decisions for themselves

## Are there limitations to guardianship?

Yes. These limitations might let a person make decisions in certain areas, but not others. The court gives a list of the limitations with the Decree and Order paperwork.

There are some situations that need more permission from the Probate and Family Court. These include:

- Major surgery involving general anesthesia
- Being admitted to a residential (live-in) facility
- Being given antipsychotic medications or needing complex medical treatment

## How does guardianship affect health care?

Guardianship affects how information is written in medical records. It also affects how medical decisions are made and who the care team can talk to.

- **Documentation in medical records.** The care team needs a copy of the most recent guardianship paperwork. This paperwork is kept in the medical record.
- **Medical decisions.** The care team follows the process for medical decision-making written in the guardianship paperwork. As the guardian, you must tell the care team if anything changes.
- **Communication.** The care team follows the process for communicating written in the guardianship paperwork. As the guardian, you must tell the care team if anything changes.

## Types of legal guardians

There are many types of legal guardians. Each type has its own set of rules listed in the Letters of Appointment and Decree and Order. The most common types are:

- **Plenary** — also called a full or general guardian. A plenary can make all medical care decisions for an adult.
- **Limited guardian** — can only make decisions that are authorized by the court and listed in the paperwork.
- **Temporary guardian** — the court can name a temporary guardian in an emergency when there is a strong chance that an adult can make their own decisions in the future. Courts decide on a temporary guardian on a case-by-case basis.
- **Co-guardian** — shares guardianship with another legal guardian.
- **Rogers Monitor** — responsible for following the court-approved treatment plan for the use of antipsychotic medication prescribed to the person under guardianship.
- **Guardian ad Litem (GAL)** — reports to the court on any recommendations related to future guardianship decisions.
- **Guardianship of a minor** — the court might name a legal guardian for a child under 18 whose parents cannot or will not make medical decisions. This guardian makes decisions about the child's health, education, and safety.

## Alternatives to guardianship

Decisions about a person's health care, wellbeing, personal items, or finances may legally be made by someone other than the person, their parent, or legal guardian.

These alternatives include:

- **Health care proxy.** An adult can name someone else (called an *agent*) to make health care decisions when they temporarily cannot do so.
- **Durable Power of Attorney (DPOA).** A person named as DPOA can make certain legal and financial decisions for the person who names them. A DPOA is just for legal and financial decisions — it cannot be used to make health care decisions.
- **Conservator.** A conservator manages the finances, property, and belongings of a person who needs financial protection. They also make legal decisions. The conservator must be named by the Probate and Family Court. A person can be a conservator and a guardian at the same time. A conservator who is not also a guardian cannot make medical decisions.

## Where can I learn more about guardianship?

- Your lawyer or legal team
- [Massachusetts laws on guardianship and conservatorship](https://www.mass.gov/topics/guardianship)
- [Probate and Family Court Forms](https://www.mass.gov/info-details/probate-and-family-court-forms)
- [Massachusetts Guardianship Association](https://massguardianshipassociation.org/)

---

*Rev. 3/2018. This document is intended to provide health-related information so that you may be better informed. It is not a substitute for a doctor's medical advice and should not be relied upon for treatment for specific medical conditions.*

en.description: Apps and phone tricks to help you remember when to take your medicine, especially once you're managing it on your own.

content.markdown:
As you become more independent, you may need to take your medicine without your parents reminding you. College, work, and being away from home can make it difficult to remember. It can also be difficult to remember your medicine if you are feeling well.

This resource offers smartphone apps that remind you to take your medicine.

## Why set up smartphone reminders?

- Cell phone reminders help people remember to take their medicine.
- Reminders decrease the rate of health complications.

## How do smartphone reminders work?

- If you have a calendar app on your phone, you can program it to send texts to you at the times you need to take your medicine. These texts can be labeled with the names of your medicines and the dosages. There are also dedicated apps that send you text reminders.
- Some apps include back-up alerts to a parent or any other person of your choice. These alerts are sent only if you do not check in after receiving your text reminder.
- Some apps keep track of how often you check in, so you can print and give the record to your doctor.
- Some apps remind you to refill your prescription.

## Free smartphone apps

- [**Medisafe Virtual Pillbox**](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.medisafe.android.client) — Google Play
- [**Pill Monitor**](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/pill-monitor-drug-minder/id485247638) — Apple App Store

Other apps can be found by searching the App Store or Google Play for terms like *"medication reminder"*.

## How can I make my reminders private?

Give your medicine reminders **code names** if you are concerned about other people seeing your reminders. Keep a key of what the messages mean in a separate, safe place.

title: Navigating Relationships with a Chronic Illness

en.description: How a chronic illness can shape your relationships with friends, family, and partners — and how to handle the conversations.

content.markdown:
Sometimes your medical problems can affect other parts of your life. This may come up with friends, family, and dating. Read more to learn how you can enjoy your various relationships.

## Friends

When deciding whether to tell a friend about your medical condition, think about:

- Your personality type and what feels comfortable to you
- Your friend's personality
- The closeness and type of friendship you share

Friends can be a great source of support. They will often feel grateful that you've chosen to tell them something so personal.

However, some friends may not understand the health challenges you have to deal with, and this can make it tough to connect with them. When people make insensitive comments, they may not understand, they may be afraid, or they may not know what to do. Sometimes sharing your experience with them may help them understand and make it easier for them to ask you questions.

People may still not get it. If this happens, only you will know whether it's a relationship to keep or one that is better to let go of. This can be hard. Your family or healthcare team — doctor, psychiatrist, nutritionist, social worker — can help you sort this out.

For the most part, though, friends can be a great source of support, and will often be really impressed by how much you're juggling.

## Family

Typically parents are very involved when you are first diagnosed with a medical condition as a kid or teenager. This is because your parents want to make sure you're safe and as healthy as you can be. It's also because your medical team asked them to make sure you took your medications, ate a healthy diet, and made it to your medical appointments.

Many young adults find it helpful to have family members continue to support them with their care. The downside, however, is that your parents can seem over-protective, or you might become too dependent.

Parents may still want to know what's going on with your care. After all, they're your parents — so they naturally worry and want the best for you. Sometimes their "nagging" comes from a place of caring concern, and that's important to keep in mind. When you're starting to feel frustrated, try talking to your parents. Being open about your feelings can sometimes avoid arguments. Your confidence and good decision-making can have a big impact on helping to ease your parents' concerns.

In addition to your parents, it can be helpful to talk to brothers and sisters. When someone has a medical condition it can affect the entire family — including your siblings, who may be going through their own range of emotions. Siblings often feel more protective of you, closer to you, and may really understand what you're dealing with. They may also feel guilt, anger, fear, or feel like they're being ignored. Talking to your siblings directly may help you have a better understanding of where each of you is coming from.

And don't forget that your healthcare team can help you as well.

## Dating

Just like with friends, you may struggle with if, when, or what to say about your medical condition to someone you're dating. There may be physical signs that you worry the person you are dating may see. This might make you feel insecure and less confident about yourself.

Ultimately, the person who decides what to tell their partner is **you**. Trust yourself. You will have a sense for when it's time. Your partner doesn't need all the details — only as much as you're comfortable sharing. And just as you needed time to understand your condition, try to allow them the same.

And don't forget: your family and healthcare team are there for you at any point along the way.
